paper.title: AutoAgent: Evolving Cognition and Elastic Memory Orchestration for Adaptive Agents
paper.central_claim: AutoAgent: a multi-agent framework in which prompt-level cognition (tool profiles, skill library, peer profiles), contextual action selection and an Elastic Memory Orchestrator are coupled by a closed-loop cognitive evolution that updates cognition and skills without retraining, giving consistent gains in task success, tool-use efficiency and collaborative robustness over static and memory-augmented baselines.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref not exposed to the worker; model type per claude-kimi config (haiku slot -> claude-sonnet-5-5[1m]).

evidence.quote: agents operate with a fixed, human-specified cognition. Tools, peers, and contexts are described by static, hand-written functional prompts that cannot be updated through experience.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: the changed non-weight object is the hand-written tool/peer/context descriptions.

evidence.quote: Evolution here is not about retraining the underlying LLM’s parameters, but about systematically updating the structured, prompt-level descriptions that constitute the agent’s actionable knowledge
evidence.support_explanation: Retained object is non-weight prompt-level cognition, so the paper is in scope.

evidence.quote: A dedicated LLM-based analyzer compares what the agent aimed to achieve (the intention) with what actually occurred (the outcome).
evidence.support_explanation: Candidate edits come from an LLM-judged intention-outcome diff; the outcome signal and its ground truth are not specified.

evidence.quote: These proposed updates—framed as revisions to descriptive text—are validated (e.g., for consistency) before being integrated into the respective cognition store.
evidence.support_explanation: The only stated retention gate is a consistency validation; no marginal-gain test, versioning or rollback.

evidence.quote: This composite description is then formalized and integrated into the agent’s Internal Cognition as a new, reusable tool.
evidence.support_explanation: Frequent successful action sequences become composite tools; admission rule and threshold are not quantified.

evidence.quote: All reported results are based on a single run per task instance under this standardized configuration.
evidence.support_explanation: Single run, no variance or seeds.

evidence.quote: the maximum number of reasoning/action steps is capped at 5
evidence.support_explanation: Same step cap for all systems on RAG and tool tasks (budget parity), but evolution and memory LLM calls are not counted.

evidence.quote: Experimental results demonstrate that the EMO module yields significant improvements over the version without EMO across all subtasks
evidence.support_explanation: Memory-orchestrator on/off ablation with DeepSeek-R1 on GAIA/HLE (Table 4: GAIA all 45.5 to 52.1; HLE all 19.2 to 28.2).

evidence.quote: we design a controlled perturbation experiment on the first 50 GAIA questions
evidence.support_explanation: The only evolved-vs-initial cognition ablation is a synthetic 50% tool-failure setting on 50 questions; whether the evolution data overlap these questions is unstated.

evidence.quote: For Python code generation and execution, the gains are larger: F1 rises from 25.55% to 37.31% (+11.76), and EM increases from 24.00% to 36.00% (+12.00).
evidence.support_explanation: Positive evolved-cognition effect in the synthetic setting; supports the mechanism but with n=50 and no variance.

evidence.quote: We ablate key components, including: (a) dynamic cognition updates, (b) elastic compression, (c) skill distillation, and (d) self-evolution.
evidence.support_explanation: Four ablations announced; results given only for elastic compression and a synthetic cognition-update test; skill distillation and self-evolution on main benchmarks are not reported.

evidence.quote: with particularly strong performance on DeepSeek-R1 (48.5% overall, 7.3 points higher than ReAct)
evidence.support_explanation: Table 3 lists AutoAgent GAIA-all 52.1 and ReAct 41.2 for DeepSeek-R1, so text and table disagree.

evidence.quote: On DeepSeek-R1, its overall score (15.2%) surpasses ReAct’s 14.4%
evidence.support_explanation: Table 3 lists AutoAgent HLE-all 28.2 for DeepSeek-R1, so narrative numbers do not match the table.
Benchmark described differently from Sec 8.1 (hierarchical task planning); benchmark identity is inconsistently reported.

evidence.quote: Results demonstrate consistent and significant improvements in task completion rate, tool-use efficiency, and collaborative robustness compared to static agents and prior memory-augmented systems.
evidence.support_explanation: Central claim; tool-use efficiency and collaborative robustness are not backed by reported numbers in Tables 1-5.

evidence.quote: we plan to incorporate richer learning signals for self-evolution, including verifier feedback and environment-specific rewards.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors acknowledge the current self-evolution signal is limited.

evidence.quote: These methods—including iterative self-evolution—remain largely episodic and task-specific, and do not explicitly couple reflection with a persistent cognitive state, elastic memory compression, and multi-agent collaboration.
evidence.support_explanation: Stated residual versus Reflexion, EvolveSearch, Voyager; uncited lineages (tool-documentation refinement, workflow memory) are not discussed.

gap.author_gap: Agents use fixed human-specified cognition, rigid workflows and inefficient context management.
gap.checked_gap: Static tool descriptions are a real, previously fixed non-weight object, but the paper gives no measurement showing misuse due to stale descriptions on its own benchmarks except the synthetic instability test.
gap.lineage_closest_adjacent: Cited: Reflexion, Voyager, MemGPT, MemInsight, EvolveSearch (paper Sec 2, v1). Uncited by us as possible neighbours (our_inference, not verified here): tool-documentation refinement from experience and workflow/skill-memory induction; no external search was possible.
gap.residue: Peer-profile evolution and joint cognition-plus-memory loop are the claimed delta; neighbours on tool-description refinement not compared.
gap.stakes: Repeated tool misuse and context bloat; asserted, quantified only in Table 5 and Table 4.
gap.method_response: LLM-driven revision of tool/peer/skill text plus elastic memory.
gap.remaining_gap: No evidence that evolved cognition persists or transfers to later tasks outside synthetic setting; admission/rollback missing.
unresolved: Overlap between evolution tasks and evaluation tasks

G.reason: Static tool/peer descriptions are a real, named fixed object with several cited neighbours, but residual versus tool-description refinement lineage is not examined and brittleness is shown only synthetically.

M.reason: Intention-outcome analysis to targeted description edits is a concrete chain with one discriminating test (tool instability), but attribution assumption and acceptance rule are weak.

X.reason: Loop and interfaces are described, but gating beyond consistency, versioning, rollback, evolution trigger, selector and composite thresholds are unspecified; code not released.

E.measurement.reason: Standard benchmarks but LLM-judge scoring unvalidated, and narrative numbers contradict Table 3 (48.5 vs 52.1; 15.2 vs 28.2) with HLE inconsistently described.

E.causality.reason: Memory ablation exists and a synthetic evolved-vs-initial test; but self-evolution, skill distillation and composites are unablated on the main benchmarks and baselines differ architecturally.

E.holdout.reason: No evolution/evaluation split, task order, or overlap statement for evolved cognition is given.

E.statistics.reason: Sample counts partly given (HLE-500, first 50 GAIA) and some negative results reported, but single run and no uncertainty.

E.cost.reason: Step and token caps matched across systems, but no token, latency or LLM-call counts for evolution or EMO despite efficiency claims.
